items.stem: Which of the following best describes "standard form"?
options: The form y = ax² + bx + c; c is the y-intercept
A line that touches a curve at exactly one point; for a line and a parabola the resulting quadratic has Δ = 0
A quadratic model h(t) = −½gt² + ut + h₀ for the height of an object moving under gravity
The vertical line x = h through the vertex of a parabola; also x = −b/(2a)
items.answer: The form y = ax² + bx + c; c is the y-intercept
items.markingKey: A. "standard form" is the form y = ax² + bx + c; c is the y-intercept.

items.stem: Explain the difference between factorised form and vertex form.
items.answer: Vertex form a(x − h)² + k shows the turning point; factorised form a(x − p)(x − q) shows the x-intercepts.
items.markingKey: Vertex form a(x − h)² + k shows the turning point; factorised form a(x − p)(x − q) shows the x-intercepts. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: "The vertex of y = (x + 4)² − 2 is (4, −2)." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: x + 4 = x − (−4), so h = −4: the vertex is (−4, −2).
items.markingKey: x + 4 = x − (−4), so h = −4: the vertex is (−4, −2). 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Factorise y = 2x² − 128 and hence find where the graph crosses the x-axis and the coordinates of its vertex.
items.answer: y = 2(x + 8)(x − 8); crosses at x = −8, 8; vertex (0, −128)
items.markingKey: Correct factorisation (M1 A1); roots (A1); vertex at x = 0 (A1).

items.stem: Write y = 3x² + 24x + 59 in the form a(x − h)² + k, and state the vertex and the minimum value of y.
items.answer: y = 3(x + 4)² + 11; vertex (−4, 11); minimum 11
items.markingKey: Factor out 3, then half the x-coefficient: h = −4 (M1); y = 3(x + 4)² + 11 (A1); vertex (−4, 11) and min 11 (A1).

items.stem: A parabola has vertex (−2, 2) and passes through (−4, 6). Find its equation in vertex form.

A water jet in a fountain in Hanoi follows y = −1(x − 2)² + 5, where x m is the horizontal distance from the nozzle. (a) State the form of this equation. (b) Find the maximum height and where it occurs. (c) Find the height of the nozzle (x = 0). (d) Find where the water hits the ground (y = 0).
items.answer: (a) y = −1(x − 2)² + 5 (b) 5 m at 2 m from the nozzle (c) 1 m (d) x = 2 + √(5) ≈ 4.24 m
items.markingKey: (a) y = −1(x − 2)² + 5 (b) 5 m at 2 m from the nozzle (c) 1 m (d) x = 2 + √(5) ≈ 4.24 m. Appropriate form chosen and features identified (A1 A1); algebra correct (M1 A1); conclusion justified or generalised (B/D: R1 C1).

items.stem: A bridge arch in Lima is a parabola that meets the ground at x = 0 and x = 36 m and has a maximum height of 15 m. (a) Write its equation in factorised form. (b) Write it in vertex form. (c) Find the height 15 m from one end. (d) Explain, using symmetry, where else the arch has the same height.
items.answer: (a) y = −(5/108)x(x − 36) (b) y = −(5/108)(x − 18)² + 15 (c) 14.6 m (d) the arch is symmetric, so the height is the same 6 m further along, at x = 21
items.markingKey: (a) y = −(5/108)x(x − 36) (b) y = −(5/108)(x − 18)² + 15 (c) 14.6 m (d) the arch is symmetric, so the height is the same 6 m further along, at x = 21. Appropriate form chosen and features identified (A1 A1); algebra correct (M1 A1); conclusion justified or generalised (B/D: R1 C1).

items.stem: State the vertex of y = −2(x + 3)² + 9.
items.markingKey: C. y = a(x − h)² + k has vertex (h, k) = (−3, 9).

items.stem: State what is meant by the term "factorised form".
items.answer: The form y = a(x − p)(x − q); p and q are the x-intercepts (roots)
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: the form y = a(x − p)(x − q); p and q are the x-intercepts (roots). Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Explain what the value of c tells you in y = ax² + bx + c.
items.answer: Setting x = 0 gives y = c, so c is the y-intercept.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Setting x = 0 gives y = c, so c is the y-intercept. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain why y = (x − 3)² + 5 does not cross the x-axis.
items.answer: (x − 3)² ≥ 0, so y ≥ 5 > 0 for every x: the minimum value is 5, above the axis.
items.markingKey: Square non-negative (R1); minimum above axis (R1).

items.stem: For y = −2(x + 5)(x + 2), find the x-intercepts, the y-intercept, the axis of symmetry and the vertex.
items.answer: x-intercepts −5 and −2; y-intercept −20; x = −7/2; vertex (−7/2, 9/2)
items.markingKey: Roots (A1); y-intercept a·p·q = −20 (A1); axis halfway (M1 A1); vertex y-value by substitution (A1).

items.stem: A parabola has vertex (−5, −6) and passes through (−8, 21). Find its equation in vertex form.
Write y = −x² + 4x − 10 in the form a(x − h)² + k, and state the vertex and the maximum value of y.
items.answer: y = −(x − 2)² − 6; vertex (2, −6); maximum −6
items.markingKey: Factor out -1, then half the x-coefficient: h = 2 (M1); y = −(x − 2)² − 6 (A1); vertex (2, −6) and max −6 (A1).

items.stem: A bridge arch in Mexico City is a parabola that meets the ground at x = 0 and x = 36 m and has a maximum height of 12 m. (a) Write its equation in factorised form. (b) Write it in vertex form. (c) Find the height 5 m from one end. (d) Explain, using symmetry, where else the arch has the same height.
items.answer: (a) y = −(1/27)x(x − 36) (b) y = −(1/27)(x − 18)² + 12 (c) 5.74 m (d) the arch is symmetric, so the height is the same 26 m further along, at x = 31
items.markingKey: (a) y = −(1/27)x(x − 36) (b) y = −(1/27)(x − 18)² + 12 (c) 5.74 m (d) the arch is symmetric, so the height is the same 26 m further along, at x = 31. Appropriate form chosen and features identified (A1 A1); algebra correct (M1 A1); conclusion justified or generalised (B/D: R1 C1).

items.stem: A water jet in a fountain in Lima follows y = −2(x − 3/2)² + 4, where x m is the horizontal distance from the nozzle. (a) State the form of this equation. (b) Find the maximum height and where it occurs. (c) Find the height of the nozzle (x = 0). (d) Find where the water hits the ground (y = 0).
items.markingKey: (a) y = −2(x − 3/2)² + 4 (b) 4 m at 3/2 m from the nozzle (c) −1/2 m (d) x = 3/2 + √(2) ≈ 2.91 m. Appropriate form chosen and features identified (A1 A1); algebra correct (M1 A1); conclusion justified or generalised (B/D: R1 C1).

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "Δ = b² − 4ac; it decides the number of real roots: Δ > 0 two, Δ = 0 one (repeated), Δ < 0 none"?
options: quadratic formula
standard form
discriminant
tangent line
items.answer: discriminant
items.markingKey: C. This is the definition of discriminant.

items.stem: Explain how a sketch helps to solve x² − x − 6 ≥ 0.
items.answer: The parabola opens upwards with roots −2 and 3; it is on or above the axis outside the roots, so x ≤ −2 or x ≥ 3.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: The parabola opens upwards with roots −2 and 3; it is on or above the axis outside the roots, so x ≤ −2 or x ≥ 3. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: A student claims: "x² > 9 means x > 3." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Also x < −3, since (−4)² = 16 > 9.
items.markingKey: Also x < −3, since (−4)² = 16 > 9. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Solve x² − 4x − 32 ≤ 0.
items.markingKey: Roots x = −4, 8 (M1 A1); parabola opens up, so the required region is between the roots: −4 ≤ x ≤ 8 (A1).

items.stem: Solve x² − 9 > 0.
items.answer: x < −3 or x > 3
items.markingKey: Roots x = −3, 3 (M1 A1); parabola opens up, so the required region is outside the roots: x < −3 or x > 3 (A1).

items.stem: A rectangular vegetable plot in Accra is 3 m longer than it is wide and has an area of 88 m². Let the width be x m. (a) Write an equation for the area. (b) Rearrange and solve it. (c) State the dimensions and explain why one solution is rejected. (d) Find the length of fencing needed to go round it.
items.answer: (a) x(x + 3) = 88 (b) x² + 3x − 88 = 0 → (x − 8)(x + 11) = 0 (c) x = 8: 8 m by 11 m (reject x = −11) (d) perimeter 38 m
items.markingKey: (a) x(x + 3) = 88 (b) x² + 3x − 88 = 0 → (x − 8)(x + 11) = 0 (c) x = 8: 8 m by 11 m (reject x = −11) (d) perimeter 38 m. Equation or condition formed (M1 A1); solved correctly (A1 A1); solutions interpreted and checked in context (D/B: R1 C1).

items.stem: State what is meant by the term "quadratic formula".
items.answer: The formula x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / (2a) gives the roots of ax² + bx + c = 0
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: the formula x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / (2a) gives the roots of ax² + bx + c = 0. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Sana solves (x − 5)(x + 1) = 8 by writing x − 5 = 8 or x + 1 = 8. Explain the mistake.
items.answer: The zero-product property only applies when the product is 0. Expand and rearrange to x² − 4x − 13 = 0 first.
items.markingKey: Zero-product condition (R1); correct method (A1).

items.stem: Sana says the solution of x² > 9 is x > 3. Explain why this is incomplete.
items.answer: Negative numbers also have squares greater than 9, e.g. (−4)² = 16; the solution is x < −3 or x > 3.
items.markingKey: Counter-example (R1); full solution (A1).

items.stem: A student claims: "If (x − 3)(x + 2) = 6, then x − 3 = 6 or x + 2 = 6." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: The zero-product rule only works when the product is 0; expand and rearrange first.
items.markingKey: The zero-product rule only works when the product is 0; expand and rearrange first. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Solve 3x² + 7x − 2 = 0, giving exact answers in simplest surd form.
"If (x − 3)(x + 2) = 6, then x − 3 = 6 or x + 2 = 6." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: The zero-product rule only works when the product is 0; expand and rearrange first.
items.markingKey: The zero-product rule only works when the product is 0; expand and rearrange first. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: A park in Singapore has a 24 m by 16 m lawn. A path of constant width x m is built around it with an area of 128 m². (a) Write an equation in x. (b) Write it in the form ax² + bx + c = 0. (c) Solve it to find the width of the path to 3 s.f. (d) Explain why one solution is rejected.
items.answer: (a) (L + 2x)(W + 2x) − 384 = 128 (b) 4x² + 80x − 128 = 0 (c) x ≈ 1.49 m (d) the negative root is meaningless for a width
items.markingKey: (a) (L + 2x)(W + 2x) − 384 = 128 (b) 4x² + 80x − 128 = 0 (c) x ≈ 1.49 m (d) the negative root is meaningless for a width. Equation or condition formed (M1 A1); solved correctly (A1 A1); solutions interpreted and checked in context (D/B: R1 C1).

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "substitution"?
options: The vertical line x = h through the vertex of a parabola; also x = −b/(2a)
Finding the maximum or minimum value of a quantity, e.g. using the vertex of a quadratic model
An inequality such as ax² + bx + c > 0, solved by finding the roots and using the shape of the parabola
Replacing a variable in one equation using the expression for it from another equation
items.answer: Replacing a variable in one equation using the expression for it from another equation
items.markingKey: D. "substitution" is replacing a variable in one equation using the expression for it from another equation.

items.stem: Chloé solves y = x + 2 and y = x² + 2 and writes "x = 0 or x = 1". Explain what is missing and complete the answer.
items.answer: The y-coordinates are needed: (0, 2) and (1, 3).
items.markingKey: Missing y identified (R1); points (A1).

items.stem: Kenji writes: "Once you have found the x-values, you are finished." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Each x must be substituted back to find the matching y-value.
items.markingKey: Each x must be substituted back to find the matching y-value. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Find the coordinates of the points where the line y = −3x + 1 meets the curve y = x² − 5x − 7.
items.markingKey: x² − 5x − 7 = −3x + 1 → x² − 2x − 8 = 0 (M1); x = −2, 4 (A1); y-values from the line (A1).

items.stem: The line y = 8x + c is a tangent to the curve y = x² + 4x. Find c and the point of contact.

In a light show in Accra, a laser beam follows y = 2x + c and a curved screen is y = x² + 2. (a) Show that the beam meets the screen when x² − 2x + (2 − c) = 0. (b) Find the discriminant. (c) Find c when the beam just touches the screen. (d) Describe how many points are lit for other values of c.
items.answer: (a) x² − 2x + (2 − c) = 0 (b) Δ = 4 − 4(2 − c) (c) c = 1 (tangent) (d) c > 1: two points; c < 1: no intersection
items.markingKey: (a) x² − 2x + (2 − c) = 0 (b) Δ = 4 − 4(2 − c) (c) c = 1 (tangent) (d) c > 1: two points; c < 1: no intersection. Substitution and quadratic formed (M1 A1); solved (A1); discriminant / points interpreted (B/D: R1 R1); communication (C1).

items.stem: A line and a parabola can intersect in at most how many points?
items.markingKey: C. Substitution gives a quadratic, which has at most two roots.

items.stem: Explain how the discriminant shows whether a line is a tangent to a parabola.
items.answer: After substitution, Δ = 0 gives exactly one repeated root, so the line meets the curve at one point only.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: After substitution, Δ = 0 gives exactly one repeated root, so the line meets the curve at one point only. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Nia writes: "If the quadratic has one root, the line crosses the parabola once." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: It touches it (tangent) rather than crossing.
items.markingKey: It touches it (tangent) rather than crossing. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Find the coordinates of the points where the line y = 4x + 6 meets the curve y = 2x² − 2x − 30.
items.markingKey: 2x² − 2x − 30 = 4x + 6 → 2x² − 6x − 36 = 0 (M1); x = −3, 6 (A1); y-values from the line (A1).

items.stem: The line y = −4x + c is a tangent to the curve y = 2x² − 4x. Find c and the point of contact.
items.answer: c = 0; point (0, 0)

items.stem: Find the coordinates of the points where the line y = −4x − 8 meets the curve y = x² − 3x − 8.
items.markingKey: x² − 3x − 8 = −4x − 8 → x² + x = 0 (M1); x = −1, 0 (A1); y-values from the line (A1).

items.stem: On a map of Toronto (units km) a hill path follows y = −x² + 18x − 60 and a straight road follows y = 2x. (a) Write an equation for where they cross. (b) Solve it. (c) Find the coordinates of the crossings. (d) Find the straight-line distance between the crossings.
items.markingKey: (a) −x² + 18x − 60 = 2x (b) x = 6, 10 (c) (6, 12) and (10, 20) (d) distance = √(16 + 64) ≈ 8.94 km. Substitution and quadratic formed (M1 A1); solved (A1); discriminant / points interpreted (B/D: R1 R1); communication (C1).

items.stem: For h(t) = −4.9t² + 14.7t, the ball is at its highest when t is:
"To maximise revenue, always charge the highest possible price." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Higher prices reduce sales; revenue p × q is largest at the vertex of the quadratic.
items.markingKey: Higher prices reduce sales; revenue p × q is largest at the vertex of the quadratic. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain why a concert organiser in Melbourne should not simply raise the ticket price as high as possible to maximise revenue.
items.answer: Revenue = price × number sold; raising the price reduces the number sold, so revenue is a downward parabola with a maximum at the vertex, not at the highest price.
items.markingKey: Trade-off identified (R1); vertex as optimum (R1).

items.stem: A museum in Accra sells q = 500 − 5p tickets a day at price p cedis. Find the price that maximises daily revenue and the maximum revenue.
items.answer: p = GH₵50.00; revenue GH₵12,500.00

items.stem: The height of a water balloon in Oslo is h = −4.9t² + 25t metres after t seconds. Find the maximum height and the time at which it hits the ground.
items.answer: max 31.9 m; lands at t = 5.10 s
items.markingKey: Vertex t = 2.55 (M1), h = 31.9 m (A1); h = 0 solved with the formula, positive root (M1) t = 5.10 s (A1).

items.stem: A museum in Singapore sells q = 400 − 5p tickets a day at price p Singapore dollars. Find the price that maximises daily revenue and the maximum revenue.

In a rugby match in Vienna, the ball’s height is h = −4.9t² + 19.6t + 1.5 metres. (a) Find the maximum height and when it occurs. (b) Find the times when the ball is above 2.5 m. (c) For how long is it above that height? (d) When does it land, and what has the model ignored?
items.answer: (a) 21.1 m at 2.00 s (b) between 0.0517 s and 3.95 s (c) 3.90 s above the bar height (d) lands at 4.08 s; air resistance is ignored
items.markingKey: (a) 21.1 m at 2.00 s (b) between 0.0517 s and 3.95 s (c) 3.90 s above the bar height (d) lands at 4.08 s; air resistance is ignored. Quadratic model formed (M1 A1); vertex / roots found (A1 A1); solution interpreted and limitations discussed (D: R1 C1).

items.stem: A farm in Switzerland uses 60 m of fencing to make a rectangle divided into 3 equal pens by 2 fences parallel to the width x m. Let the length be y m. (a) Express y in terms of x. (b) Write the total area A in terms of x. (c) Find the dimensions that maximise A. (d) Find the maximum area.
items.markingKey: (a) y = (60 − 4x)/2 (b) A = x(60 − 4x)/2 (c) x = 15/2 m, y = 15 m (d) max area 225/2 m². Quadratic model formed (M1 A1); vertex / roots found (A1 A1); solution interpreted and limitations discussed (D: R1 C1).

items.stem: Explain why the vertex of a quadratic model gives its maximum or minimum.
items.answer: The parabola is symmetric and turns at the vertex; with a < 0 every other point is lower, so the vertex is the maximum.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: The parabola is symmetric and turns at the vertex; with a < 0 every other point is lower, so the vertex is the maximum. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Briefly explain why a projectile model is only valid between launch and landing.
items.answer: Before launch and after landing the object is not in flight, so the formula (e.g. negative heights) no longer describes it.

items.stem: A rectangular garden in Cairo has perimeter 50 m. Write the area in terms of the width x and find the maximum area.
items.answer: A = x(25 − x); max 156 m² when x = 12.5 m

items.stem: Explain how to find the values of c for which the line y = 2x + c meets y = x² in two points.

items.stem: Explain why vertex form is useful for finding the maximum or minimum value.
items.answer: (x − h)² ≥ 0, so a(x − h)² + k is smallest (a > 0) or largest (a < 0) when x = h, giving the value k directly.

items.answer: The formula contains √Δ: a positive Δ gives two different values (±), zero gives one, and a negative Δ has no real square root.

items.stem: Ingrid writes: "To maximise revenue, always charge the highest possible price." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Higher prices reduce sales; revenue p × q is largest at the vertex of the quadratic.
items.markingKey: Higher prices reduce sales; revenue p × q is largest at the vertex of the quadratic. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Solve x² − 6x − 16 < 0.
items.markingKey: Roots x = −2, 8 (M1 A1); parabola opens up, so the required region is between the roots: −2 < x < 8 (A1).

items.stem: The line y = 5x + c is a tangent to the curve y = x² + x. Find c and the point of contact.
items.answer: c = −4; point (2, 6)

items.stem: Write y = x² + 8x + 13 in the form a(x − h)² + k, and state the vertex and the minimum value of y.
items.answer: y = (x + 4)² − 3; vertex (−4, −3); minimum −3
items.markingKey: Half the x-coefficient: h = −4 (M1); y = (x + 4)² − 3 (A1); vertex (−4, −3) and min −3 (A1).

items.stem: The height of a stone in Dubai is h = −4.9t² + 9.8t + 10 metres after t seconds. Find the maximum height and the time at which it hits the ground.
items.answer: max 14.9 m; lands at t = 2.74 s
items.markingKey: Vertex t = 1.00 (M1), h = 14.9 m (A1); h = 0 solved with the formula, positive root (M1) t = 2.74 s (A1).

items.stem: "x² > 9 means x > 3." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Also x < −3, since (−4)² = 16 > 9.
items.markingKey: Also x < −3, since (−4)² = 16 > 9. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: "If the quadratic has one root, the line crosses the parabola once." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: It touches it (tangent) rather than crossing.
items.markingKey: It touches it (tangent) rather than crossing. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Investigate the family y = (x − h)² − 5. (a) Find the vertex for h = 1, 2, 3. (b) Describe the pattern. (c) Expand the equation in terms of h. (d) Find the roots in terms of h and show that the distance between them does not depend on h.
items.answer: (a) vertices (1, −5), (2, −5), (3, −5) (b) all vertices lie on the line y = −5; h moves the graph horizontally (c) y = x² − 2hx + h² − 5 (d) roots h ± √5, so the roots are always 2√5 = 4.47 apart
items.markingKey: (a) vertices (1, −5), (2, −5), (3, −5) (b) all vertices lie on the line y = −5; h moves the graph horizontally (c) y = x² − 2hx + h² − 5 (d) roots h ± √5, so the roots are always 2√5 = 4.47 apart. Appropriate form chosen and features identified (A1 A1); algebra correct (M1 A1); conclusion justified or generalised (B/D: R1 C1).

items.stem: A football club in Toronto sells 800 tickets at C$30. For every C$1 increase in price, 10 fewer tickets are sold. Let x be the price increase. (a) Write the revenue R in terms of x. (b) Find the value of x that maximises R. (c) Find the best price, the number of tickets and the revenue. (d) State one limitation of the model.
items.answer: (a) R = (30 + x)(800 − 10x) (b) x = 25 (c) price C$55.00, 550 tickets, revenue C$30,250.00 (d) e.g. demand may not fall linearly; capacity limits
items.markingKey: (a) R = (30 + x)(800 − 10x) (b) x = 25 (c) price C$55.00, 550 tickets, revenue C$30,250.00 (d) e.g. demand may not fall linearly; capacity limits. Quadratic model formed (M1 A1); vertex / roots found (A1 A1); solution interpreted and limitations discussed (D: R1 C1).

items.stem: A park in London has a 30 m by 20 m lawn. A path of constant width x m is built around it with an area of 150 m². (a) Write an equation in x. (b) Write it in the form ax² + bx + c = 0. (c) Solve it to find the width of the path to 3 s.f. (d) Explain why one solution is rejected.
items.answer: (a) (L + 2x)(W + 2x) − 600 = 150 (b) 4x² + 100x − 150 = 0 (c) x ≈ 1.42 m (d) the negative root is meaningless for a width
items.markingKey: (a) (L + 2x)(W + 2x) − 600 = 150 (b) 4x² + 100x − 150 = 0 (c) x ≈ 1.42 m (d) the negative root is meaningless for a width. Equation or condition formed (M1 A1); solved correctly (A1 A1); solutions interpreted and checked in context (D/B: R1 C1).

items.stem: On a map of Lima (units km) a hill path follows y = −x² + 13x − 39 and a straight road follows y = −x + 9. (a) Write an equation for where they cross. (b) Solve it. (c) Find the coordinates of the crossings. (d) Find the straight-line distance between the crossings.
items.markingKey: (a) −x² + 13x − 39 = −x + 9 (b) x = 6, 8 (c) (6, 3) and (8, 1) (d) distance = √(4 + 4) ≈ 2.83 km. Substitution and quadratic formed (M1 A1); solved (A1); discriminant / points interpreted (B/D: R1 R1); communication (C1).

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "The form y = a(x − h)² + k; the vertex (turning point) is (h, k)"?
options: vertex form
projectile model
discriminant
standard form
items.answer: vertex form
items.markingKey: A. This is the definition of vertex form.

items.stem: The maximum value of h = −5(t − 2)² + 30 is:
items.markingKey: C. The vertex is (2, 30).

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "quadratic inequality"?
options: The form y = a(x − h)² + k; the vertex (turning point) is (h, k)
An inequality such as ax² + bx + c > 0, solved by finding the roots and using the shape of the parabola
The values of the input for which the model makes sense in context, e.g. times between launch and landing
A pair of equations, one linear and one quadratic, solved by substitution to find their intersection points
items.answer: An inequality such as ax² + bx + c > 0, solved by finding the roots and using the shape of the parabola
items.markingKey: B. "quadratic inequality" is an inequality such as ax² + bx + c > 0, solved by finding the roots and using the shape of the parabola.

items.stem: Explain, using the discriminant, why the line y = −3 never meets the parabola y = x² + 1.
items.answer: x² + 1 = −3 → x² + 4 = 0, Δ = −16 < 0, so there are no real solutions.
items.markingKey: Equation formed (M1); Δ < 0 interpreted (R1).

items.stem: Explain why y = (x − 4)² + 4 does not cross the x-axis.
items.answer: (x − 4)² ≥ 0, so y ≥ 4 > 0 for every x: the minimum value is 4, above the axis.
items.markingKey: Square non-negative (R1); minimum above axis (R1).

items.stem: Explain why, for a fixed perimeter, a square gives the largest rectangular area.
items.answer: A = x(P/2 − x) is a downward parabola with vertex at x = P/4, which makes both sides equal.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: A = x(P/2 − x) is a downward parabola with vertex at x = P/4, which makes both sides equal. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Tariq solves x² = 8x by dividing by x and gets x = 8. Explain what is wrong and give the full solution.
items.answer: Dividing by x loses the root x = 0. x² − 8x = 0 → x(x − 8) = 0 → x = 0 or x = 8.
items.markingKey: Lost root explained (R1); both roots (A1).

items.stem: "Once you have found the x-values, you are finished." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Each x must be substituted back to find the matching y-value.
items.markingKey: Each x must be substituted back to find the matching y-value. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Briefly explain why the axis of symmetry of y = a(x − p)(x − q) is x = (p + q)/2.
items.answer: A parabola is symmetric about its axis, and the two roots are mirror images, so the axis lies exactly halfway between them.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: A parabola is symmetric about its axis, and the two roots are mirror images, so the axis lies exactly halfway between them. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: The height of a stone in Cape Town is h = −4.9t² + 9.8t + 5 metres after t seconds. Find the maximum height and when it occurs.
Solve −x² + 9x − 20 ≥ 0.
items.markingKey: Roots x = 4, 5 (M1 A1); parabola opens down, so the required region is between the roots: 4 ≤ x ≤ 5 (A1).

items.stem: The line y = 5x + c is a tangent to the curve y = 3x² + 3x. Find c and the point of contact.
Factorise y = −2x² + 2x + 112 and hence find where the graph crosses the x-axis and the coordinates of its vertex.
items.markingKey: Correct factorisation (M1 A1); roots (A1); vertex at x = 1/2 (A1).

items.stem: A museum in Toronto sells q = 300 − 5p tickets a day at price p Canadian dollars. Find the price that maximises daily revenue and the maximum revenue.
Freya writes: "x² > 9 means x > 3." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Also x < −3, since (−4)² = 16 > 9.
items.markingKey: Also x < −3, since (−4)² = 16 > 9. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Find the coordinates of the points where the line y = −3x + 3 meets the curve y = x² − x + 3.
items.markingKey: x² − x + 3 = −3x + 3 → x² + 2x = 0 (M1); x = −2, 0 (A1); y-values from the line (A1).

items.stem: The main cable of a suspension bridge in Oslo hangs between towers 120 m apart, 60 m above the road; its lowest point is 10 m above the road, midway. Taking x = 0 at the left tower, (a) write the cable’s equation in vertex form. (b) Find its height a quarter of the way across. (c) Find where the cable is 20 m above the road. (d) Write the equation in standard form.
items.markingKey: (a) y = (1/72)(x − 60)² + 10 (b) 22.5 m (c) x = 33.17 m and x = 86.83 m (d) y = x²/72 − 5x/3 + 60. Appropriate form chosen and features identified (A1 A1); algebra correct (M1 A1); conclusion justified or generalised (B/D: R1 C1).

items.stem: In a rugby match in Singapore, the ball’s height is h = −4.9t² + 19.6t + 0.5 metres. (a) Find the maximum height and when it occurs. (b) Find the times when the ball is above 3 m. (c) For how long is it above that height? (d) When does it land, and what has the model ignored?
items.answer: (a) 20.1 m at 2.00 s (b) between 0.132 s and 3.87 s (c) 3.74 s above the bar height (d) lands at 4.03 s; air resistance is ignored
items.markingKey: (a) 20.1 m at 2.00 s (b) between 0.132 s and 3.87 s (c) 3.74 s above the bar height (d) lands at 4.03 s; air resistance is ignored. Quadratic model formed (M1 A1); vertex / roots found (A1 A1); solution interpreted and limitations discussed (D: R1 C1).

items.stem: A café in Lisbon models its daily profit P (in hundreds of euros) from selling x litres of smoothie as P = −2(x − 9)(x − 12). (a) Expand the model. (b) Find the break-even points. (c) Solve P > 0 and interpret it. (d) Find the maximum profit and the number of litres that gives it.
items.answer: (a) P = −2x² + 42x − 216 (b) P = 0 at x = 9 and 12 (c) profit when 9 < x < 12 (d) maximum at x = 21/2: €450
items.markingKey: (a) P = −2x² + 42x − 216 (b) P = 0 at x = 9 and 12 (c) profit when 9 < x < 12 (d) maximum at x = 21/2: €450. Equation or condition formed (M1 A1); solved correctly (A1 A1); solutions interpreted and checked in context (D/B: R1 C1).

items.stem: A skateboarder in Nairobi launches a ball from the bottom of a straight ramp. The ball follows y = −(1/20)x² + x and the ramp is y = (1/2)x (metres). (a) Form an equation for where they meet. (b) Solve it. (c) Find where the ball lands on the ramp. (d) Decide whether the ball is rising or falling when it lands, with a reason.
items.answer: (a) −(1/20)x² + (1/2)x = 0 (b) x = 0 or x = 10 (c) (10, 5) (d) the vertex of the ball’s path is at x = 10, so it lands exactly at its highest point when it lands
items.markingKey: (a) −(1/20)x² + (1/2)x = 0 (b) x = 0 or x = 10 (c) (10, 5) (d) the vertex of the ball’s path is at x = 10, so it lands exactly at its highest point when it lands. Substitution and quadratic formed (M1 A1); solved (A1); discriminant / points interpreted (B/D: R1 R1); communication (C1).
